page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it is
steps.why: The tissue is defined by where it lies, because the leech coelom is reduced to channels and this tissue is what fills the rest of that space.
common_mistakes: Naming it for the earthworm. Botryoidal tissue is characteristic of leeches.
Writing that it lies in the gut. It lies in the coelomic space.
steps.memory_tip: Leech only. Botryoidal means grape-like, and the cells lie in clusters.
steps.margin_note: Which animal, where it lies, what it looks like. Three or four lines.
lines: Botryoidal tissue is a tissue found only in
In a leech the coelom is reduced to narrow
channels, and this tissue fills the space
Its brown cells lie in rounded clusters.

steps.label: Its functions
steps.why: The tissue lies in the coelomic channels themselves, which is why it can both clear waste from them and rebuild them after an injury.
common_mistakes: Giving only excretion. Three functions are expected for the full mark.
Writing that it stores food. It stores iron and calcium.
steps.memory_tip: Three jobs: clears waste, stores iron and calcium, rebuilds channels.
steps.margin_note: Three numbered functions, one line each.
lines: 3) Formation of new blood channels in a part
of the body that has been injured.

insider_note: A short question with a long answer — the second mark is for the list of three functions, not for a longer description of the tissue.
